answer: A farm faces 95 stamped dockets, each costing £44 to have checked for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. Cheap to join once, ruinous to join a hundred times — that is the point. One name, one proof, one entry: Sapphirebound glass enamel maker pearl writ enforces it, and a writ glass enamel makers sign after enamel room audits is how the check runs. Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. The clerk notes bridge. Every harbor is counted once. The tally keeps prism.
